neighbours.label: variety-of-choice words (selection, range, array, collection, variety, options) when they describe a set of offerings to choose from; 'range' or 'selection' in other senses stays quiet
fire: The bakery on the corner offers a wide selection of breads and pastries.
Their online store stocks an extensive range of camping equipment.
Guests can pick from a broad array of toppings at the salad bar.
The library has only a limited selection of foreign-language novels.
This supplier carries a wider variety of fabrics than any other in town.
The menu gives diners plenty of options for vegetarian meals.
The garden centre sells an impressive collection of roses in every colour.
Compared with last year, the catalogue has a much wider range of sizes.
quiet: The bakery on the corner sells bread and pastries every morning.
Their online store ships camping equipment within two days.
The radio has a range of about forty kilometres in open country.
Darwin argued that selection favours the better adapted individuals.
The telescope array in the desert records signals at night.
The debt collection agency sent a letter to the tenant.
The garden centre sells one red rose bush for ten pounds.
The library closes early on foreign holidays and weekends.

notes: Card: peaks on selection x5, range x3, array, wider, extensive, limited, options, all about what a shop or programme offers; the + pole direction promotes ' options', ' available', ' choices' when reversed. Probes: 'extensive collection' 0.67, 'big selection' 0.63, 'wide range of colours' 0.39, 'available options' 0.31; 'mountain range' 0.01, 'Natural selection' 0.00.
